transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've been struggling with these repetitive behaviors and urges that are starting to take over my daily life. Specifically, I feel this overwhelming need to constantly wash my hands and clean everything. It has gotten to the point where it's really hard to stop.

Do you feel that these cleaning behaviors are something you do to prevent a specific, dreaded outcome or to relieve a sense of discomfort, or are you primarily worried about a wide range of different life events and daily responsibilities?

It's definitely about trying to relieve an intense sense of discomfort and anxiety from feeling contaminated. I don't really think about general daily worries when I do it; I just have this overwhelming urge to wash away dirt and germs until it feels right.
Do you recognize these thoughts and urges as coming from your own mind, and do you find them to be intrusive or unwanted in nature?
I'm not quite sure how to describe it or where they come from, but they are definitely unwanted. I just feel a very strong, uncontrollable urge to do these actions to stop feeling so anxious.
On an average day, how much time would you say you spend performing these cleaning rituals, and how significantly do they interfere with your ability to work, socialize, or complete your daily tasks?

To be honest, I'm not sure of the exact amount of time I spend on these rituals every day because I completely lose track of time while doing them. I'm also not sure how to measure how much they interfere with my life, but it definitely makes getting through my day a lot harder.
Do you ever feel that these beliefs about germs are excessive or unreasonable, even while you are in the middle of performing the cleaning rituals?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. In the moment, the anxiety is so intense that I don't really think about whether the beliefs are reasonable or not. I just feel like I absolutely have to do it to make the discomfort go away.

latest_inference.note: The patient's clinical presentation—characterized by recurrent, unwanted urges (obsessions related to contamination) and repetitive behaviors (hand washing/cleaning) performed to alleviate intense anxiety—is highly consistent with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. The lack of insight regarding the reasonableness of the beliefs is a common feature in OCD and does not necessitate a shift to a psychotic disorder. I am confident in this diagnosis.
